title: Partial Trace as Admissible Forgetting
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in quantum information, centered on the claim that subsystem reduction erases global distinctions while preserving a declared class of local observables. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that reduced-state adequacy is relative to the observation algebra; erased correlations cannot be inferred from the reduced state alone. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: Bell-state vs maximally mixed control, local expectation preservation, and relative entropy contraction, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: Petz Recovery: Recovery Is Not Inversion
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in quantum information/operator algebras, centered on the claim that recovery depends on channel, reference state, and sufficient family rather than merely reversing an arrow. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that recoverability is conditional and typed; successful recovery does not make coarse-graining globally invertible. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: finite CPTP example, exact sufficient-family recovery, and failed Bell-correlation recovery, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: CR3BP: Hill Regions and Transport Boundaries
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in celestial mechanics/dynamical systems, centered on the claim that integrals and invariant structures define admissible regions and transport channels in phase space. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that boundary language becomes concrete dynamical geometry governing reachable transport. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: Jacobi integral, Hill-region transitions, and transport/event calibration, plus 1 additional evidence item.

title: Gauge Symmetry: Redundant Representation versus Physical Distinction
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in classical/quantum gauge theory, centered on the claim that different mathematical descriptions may encode the same physical state. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that representational difference must not be promoted to physical difference without gauge-invariant content. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: electromagnetic gauge example, gauge-invariant observable, and global/topological caveat.

title: Markov Coarse-Graining and Lumpability as Dynamically Admissible Forgetting
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in stochastic processes/statistical physics, centered on the claim that microstate distinctions may be forgotten only when the reduced future is well defined on the chosen partition. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that dynamic reduction requires stronger conditions than static observational equivalence. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: finite Markov chain, lumpable partition, and non-lumpable counterexample.

title: Effective Field Theory as Scale-Relative Forgetting
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in quantum field theory/effective theory, centered on the claim that high-resolution distinctions are integrated out while low-energy obligations survive through effective couplings. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that which distinctions matter is scale- and observable-relative, with matching conditions carrying discarded influence. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: simple heavy-field integration example, matching/power counting, and regime-of-validity firewall.

title: Gauss’s Law and Maxwell Boundary Conditions
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in electromagnetism, centered on the claim that sources, fluxes, and interface matching are connected by exact field equations and jump conditions. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that boundary/interface conditions are literal physical constraints, not metaphorical abstractions. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: integral Gauss law, interface boundary conditions, and surface charge/current examples.

title: Kron Reduction and Effective Terminal Response
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in circuits/network physics, centered on the claim that interior network variables may be eliminated while preserving externally observable terminal response. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that effective circuits provide a physical calibration of exact boundary-response reduction. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: small resistor network, Kron/Schur derivation, and terminal-equivalence check.

title: Renormalization Group Flow as Successor Effective Description
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in statistical/QFT renormalization, centered on the claim that coarse-graining changes the active effective description and its parameterization as scale changes. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that successor descriptions can be formalized without claiming one representation is fundamental at all scales. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: block-spin or simple beta-flow example, fixed points, and universality caveat.

title: Thermodynamic Coarse-Graining and Entropy
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in statistical mechanics, centered on the claim that many microstates become observationally equivalent under a macroscopic description. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that entropy and coarse variables calibrate distinction loss without identifying ignorance with ontological absence. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: macrostate partition, microstate multiplicity, and coarse-graining caveats.

title: Noether’s Theorem: Invariance and Protected Structure
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in classical/field theory, centered on the claim that lawful transformations preserving the action expose conserved structure. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that invariance has exact native semantics and should constrain generic Boundary uses of invariant. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: time translation/energy example, continuous-symmetry assumptions, and boundary-term caveat.

title: Quantum Measurement as Operational Distinction Production
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in quantum measurement/information, centered on the claim that measurement architecture determines which distinctions become operationally observable. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that POVMs, distinguishability, and coarse-grained outcomes provide native terms for observational boundaries. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: finite POVM example, indistinguishable state pair under chosen POVM, and interpretation firewall.

title: Decoherence as Environment-Induced Effective Distinction Structure
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in open quantum systems, centered on the claim that interaction with an environment changes which distinctions remain robust in a reduced description. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that decoherence explains effective observational structure without by itself resolving interpretation of measurement. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: simple dephasing channel, pointer-basis example, and measurement-problem firewall.

title: Hamiltonian Flow and Liouville’s Theorem as Lawful Transport
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in classical mechanics, centered on the claim that states move through phase space under structure-preserving dynamics. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that lawful transport can be anchored in symplectic structure and phase-volume preservation. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: harmonic oscillator flow, Liouville theorem, and dissipative contrast.

title: Scattering and the S-Matrix as Boundary Response
summary: This paper develops a Boundary First reading in quantum/field scattering, centered on the claim that interior interaction is summarized by relations between asymptotic input and output states. It translates that reading back into native terms by emphasizing that observable boundary response can replace inaccessible interior history under stated asymptotic assumptions. The proposed evidence is deliberately concrete: simple potential-scattering example, unitarity, and inverse-scattering caveat.
